newsitem.title: USA: ITT to acquire Goulds Pumps for $815 million.
newsitem.headline: ITT to acquire Goulds Pumps for $815 million.

text.p: Industrial products maker ITT Industries Inc. said Monday it will acquire Gould Pumps Inc., becoming the world's largest pump manufacturer, for $815 million.

The announcement, made before financial markets opened, pumped up Gould's stock, which surged $13.25, or 58 percent, to $36.125 in active trading on Nasdaq market, where it was the biggest percentage gainer.
Under the definitive agreement between the two companies, ITT will pay $37 a share, or about $815 million, in cash and also will assume $119 million in Goulds Pumps debt.

ITT Industries will become the leading global supplier of pumps with the acquisition of Goulds, which is based in Fairport, N.Y. Goulds is a worldwide supplier of industrial, residential and commercial pumps, parts and accessories.
"This acquisition catapults us to a solid No. 1 in the world from No. 2," Travis Engen, chairman of White Plains, N.Y.-based ITT Industries, said in an interview.
"On the revenue side, the products of ITT Industries' fluid technology business and Goulds complement each other perfectly," Engen said in a statement.

"For example, Goulds is one of the leading producers of pumps for the industrial sector while ITT Industries is a world leader in submersible pumps for municipal water treatment worldwide," Engen said.
Engen said ITT Industries fluid technology unit posted annual revenues of $1.3 billion last year, while Goulds' revenues were $775 million.

Combined, Goulds and ITT Industries fluid technology will have about $2.1 billion in annual revenue, topping Japan-based Ebara Corp.'s $1.6 billion in annual fluid technology revenues, Engen said. He estimated the overall global pump business to be worth about $15 billion annually.

Moments after the deal was annouced, Goulds said it was adopting a "poison pill" shareholder rights plan as an anti-takeover defence. It said it would terminate the plan immediately before ITT Industries acquires the company.
Engen said in the interview he was unaware of any rival suitors for Goulds. He said his company approached Goulds in March.

Engen declined to comment on whether his company acted as a "white knight" alternative to a hostile takeover, but said Goulds' poison pill gives the pump maker "the opportunity to be more in control in the next few months."
ITT Industries said it expects the acquisition to enhance earnings growth, "with an accretive impact in its first full year and significant contributions thereafter."
The cost benefits will result from greater economies in purchasing, manufacturing, marketing and sales, research and development and support functions, the company said.
ITT Industries stock rose 62.5 cents to $24 on the New York Stock Exchange.

ITT Industries also announced an 11 percent increase in first-quarter profits to $44.3 million, or 37 cents a share, from $40 million, or 33 cents a share, a year ago that topped Wall Street expectations. The consensus analyst forecast had been for 34 cents a share, according to the First Call service.

In addition to pumps, ITT Industries subsidiaries make automotive brake and chassis systems, electronic warfare systems, radar equipment and valves. It was created in 1995 when ITT Corp. split into three companies.
One arbitrageur said Goulds' announcement of the "poison pill" soon after the merger announcement was "atypical, but not unheard of."
"It seems Goulds has been shopped around for several years. The price seems rich so maybe there was someone else, amid some aggressive bidding," the arbitrageur said.
NatWest Securities analyst Thomas Burns said Goulds "got a great price."
"If I were the CFO of Goulds, I would go home and pull myself a glass of scotch," Burns said.
